assertions: Every canonical objection and rebuttal act produces one bounded relation record.
Objection relations distinguish content, evidence, wording, definition, procedure, attribution, premise, relevance, general, and unresolved dimensions.
Rebuttal relations retain direct, denial, counterevidence, counterexample, alternative-explanation, qualification, scope-correction, causal-challenge, and unresolved methods.
Exact normalized targets take precedence over temporal candidates.
A single act in the nearest prior bounded-context utterance is probable and review-required.
Multiple acts in the nearest prior utterance remain alternative targets.
An explicitly unresolved rebuttal cannot be promoted by temporal proximity.
Supporting and challenged evidence spans remain source-addressed.
Rebuttal classification never establishes rebuttal success.
Every canonical concession act produces a concession structure.
Partial concession retains restrictions expressed by same-utterance qualifications.
Every canonical qualification act produces a qualification structure.
Qualifications preserve scope, temporal, conditional, probabilistic, exception, limitation, hedging, precision, category, and threshold dimensions.
Several compatible same-utterance targets remain ambiguous qualification scope.
No factual adjudication or intent inference is performed.
Argument-relation run and report artifacts are sealed, replayable, and reusable.
CLI operations build, validate, inspect, and list objections, rebuttals, concessions, qualifications, and unresolved relations.
Schema export includes all six argument-relation contracts.
limitations: Temporal proximity is a conservative candidate-target heuristic, not semantic proof.
Retained disagreement is limited to exact source spans available through canonical acts.
The controlled fixtures qualify construction mechanics, not natural-conversation relational accuracy.
